sections.html:
Greenacres sellers can go through an agent, handle the sale personally, or accept cash from someone who will deal with the repairs. Speed, repair cost and certainty rarely all point the same way.

  • Agent listing: wider reach, paid for with showings and a lender's calendar.
  • Direct sale: you hold the price and the paperwork.
  • Cash: few conditions, flexible timing, repairs priced in.

Collect written bids and work out what each would put in your hands once payoffs, tax and recording are paid.

Greenacres is a compact city in central Palm Beach County, about six square miles. Developer Lawrence Carter Swain platted half the townsite in 1923 and began selling lots in 1925 for $225 with $45 down, aiming at working families. The city was incorporated in 1926 as the Town of Greenacres City, lost its charter after a petition in 1944, regained its rights in December 1945 and reincorporated in 1947.

Today about 44,736 people live here, and the city is dense, with 7,407 people per square mile. That working-family history still shows in the housing: family-sized homes on small lots.

About two thirds of homes here are lived in by their owners (66.5 percent for 2020 to 2024), at a median value of $291,000. Rent runs $1,756 at the median, and monthly owner costs median $1,865 with a mortgage and $672 without. Households average 2.90 people, and 15,249 households were counted.

Shoppers measure your price against what they pay today. Many are first-time buyers or growing families who weigh bedrooms and yard space above finishes. A clean house ready for move-in shows well, while an unrepaired one needs a discount.

Conversations in this city often happen in more than one language. Provide documents in clear form, use a translator or a bilingual closing agent if the buyer asks, and keep offers in writing. A plain purchase agreement prevents misunderstandings that cost time at title. Buyers who commute along the coast also like to hear about road access, so mention the nearest major roads and shopping.

A deed in Palm Beach County is taxed at 70 cents per $100 of consideration, paid to the clerk at recording. Under section 201.02(1)(a), a mortgage on the property is part of the consideration. Each party to the deed carries liability for the tax, whoever promised to pay it.

Recording is billed by the page under s. 28.24(13): $5.00 for the first and $4.00 for each after it, with trust fund and technology charges on top. Look for the totals on your settlement statement.

Assessed value is fixed each January 1, and the county appraiser mails a notice of proposed taxes in August. A challenge to that value is a petition to the clerk, due within 25 days. The November bill carries a 4 percent discount that declines to 1 percent in February, and April 1 begins delinquency. File homestead and other exemptions by March 1.

  • Homestead takes up to $50,000 off value, and the extra $25,000 slice skips school taxes.
  • Save Our Homes caps yearly assessed growth at the smaller of 3 percent and inflation.
  • Once you sell, the following January 1 resets the assessment to market-based value.

Phone the tax collector for the exact balance and file the written figure with your closing papers, so you can check the settlement statement against it.

State law sets a timeline for each of these.

  • Inherited: summary administration, a streamlined probate, covers estates that are small or long past death (s. 735.201).
  • Foreclosure: the clerk auctions the property soon after final judgment, and bidders post a deposit (s. 45.031).
  • Tenant: a monthly tenancy needs 30 days' notice (s. 83.57).

About a third of Greenacres units are renter-occupied, so tenant questions come up often. Share the lease with any buyer at the outset.

sections.h2: What to line up before closing
sections.html:
Missing records delay more closings than buyers do, so gather them early.

  • The deed, or trust or probate papers that show who can sign.
  • Payoff statements from every lender.
  • Permit and repair records for roof, electrical and air conditioning work.
  • Lease copies and rent history for tenants.
  • The newest TRIM notice and tax bill.

A deed needs two subscribing witnesses under s. 689.01, so schedule the signing with your title agent.

When a written offer is accepted, the title company looks for liens and back taxes, asks for payoffs and picks the closing date. You sign the contract, and later the deed in front of two witnesses. Payoffs, stamp tax and recording come out of the proceeds, and the rest goes to you. With no appraisal or loan underwriting, a cash closing can move fast. Ask the buyer to commit the date and the cost split to paper, and do not pay anyone before closing.

sections.h2: Listing or cash: weighing the trade
sections.html: Listing can bring a higher number, but it asks for patience through showings, inspection requests, a buyer's loan and carrying costs while you wait. Cash gives you speed and certainty and leaves repairs to the buyer, so the price reflects that work. A tidy house with a flexible date may do well on the market. A house needing work, with a tenant or a lender deadline, often fits a direct sale better. Ask for at least two written offers and rank them by net proceeds.

sections.h2: If an inheritance or unpaid taxes complicate things
sections.html: Talk to the clerk's probate office or a probate attorney about who may sign for an estate, and send the title company any court papers the moment you have them. If taxes are owed, the payoff comes out of your proceeds at closing, so ask the tax collector for a written figure early. Neither problem has to stop a sale, but both are easier to solve with weeks of lead time than with days. Starting those calls before you accept an offer also lets you give a buyer a realistic closing date from the beginning.

The title agent goes over the settlement statement with you. Read every line, ask about any charge you do not recognize and confirm that payoffs match your letters. After the deed is signed and recorded, hand over keys and remotes and expect your proceeds by wire or check. Afterward, update your mailing address with the property appraiser and keep copies of what you signed, including the final settlement statement.

faqs.a: Yes, at 66.5 percent for 2020 to 2024, which suggests most buyers plan to live in the house.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Greenacres?
faqs.a: $291,000 for 2020 to 2024. It is only a rough guide, because a house with a new roof and one needing work can sit far apart. Ask for written offers on your own property.
In 1926 as the Town of Greenacres City. It lost its charter in a 1944 petition, was reinstated in December 1945 and reincorporated in 1947.

faqs.q: Who pays doc stamp tax on a Greenacres deed?
faqs.a: The statute makes every party liable. The contract decides who actually pays, and the closing agent collects at recording.

faqs.q: When must I file homestead after buying in Greenacres?
faqs.a: Send DR-501 to the county property appraiser by March 1 of the tax year. You must own and live in the home as of January 1.
